div.head: VOLUNTEERS AT DELAMERE. -- Interesting Operations.
div.p: VOLUNTEERS AT DELAMERE. -- Interesting Operations.

On Saturday about 90 members of the Warrington Volunteer Batzalion who were unable to attend the camp on Salisbury Plain in July, lett the town for a week's encampment at Delamere Forest. A number of men connected with the Mounted Infantry and the Cycligt Companies and the transport section paraded at the Drill Hall at two o'clock in toe afternoon, sod pro- ceeded by road to Delamere and the other members of the battalion travelled by raildeavicg the Central Station at 3.30. Major Roome(adjutant) and Captain Ml:cocks were in command.

The Warrington Volunteers in camp form part of a composite body of all branches of the service including the 4th Provisional Battalion from Lichfield, No 1 Com- pany North-western District Mounted Infantry, 96th Battery Royal Artillery from Birmingham, the Provi- sional Battalion of Dragoons (composed of the let Dragoons and 3rd and 6th Dragoon Guards), details of Volunteers from Liverpool, the King's Royal Rifles, let South Lancashire Volunteers, and 10 troopers per squad- ron of the Earl of Chester's Imperial Yeomanry Cavalry. With the eaceptioa of the mounted infantry (Manchester) who have been undergoing training near Delmore Station for a month past, all these regiments formed camp at Kingswood, hard by the new Liverpool and Manchester Sanatoria, on Saturday. Major-General Flallsen-Parr, who has personally supervised the maneeuvres, took up his quarters with his staff, at Kingswood, whlle other offiaers have been quartered at the Bungalow, at Dela- mere. The manceavres during the week have been the most extensive ever carried out in Cheshire. After a quiet week-end the entire camp was alive at an early hour on Monday in preparation for an elaborate specimen of mimic warfare. Each branch was kept in iartorance of the other's intentions, but the command- ing officers formulated a scheme of operations, the general idea of which was*as follows :--A hoqile raiding force ;Blue) had effected a landing in North Wales, and bad acted with such suddenness that they had actually captured the passages of the Dee at Chester and were victoriously marching for waad with a view to striking a blow at Manchester and the Ship Canal, A Red force was concentrated at Northwich, ani, being apprised of the movement, marched out towards Delamere Forest with a view to intercept and scatter the enemy. The Blues passed on from Chester to Tlelsby, where the war- fare actually commenced. The home defenders di,- covered the Blues in the neighbourhood of Dalarnere, and reconnoitring having taken place an engaacrnent occured at Mouldswerth. The defenders held the railway bridge, at Mouldworth Station, and the invading force, commenced an attack and presumably drove the Reds from their position and blew up the railway. The Blues brought two 15-pounders of the Royal Artillery to bear upon the home force, cover being taken along the line of hills separating Delamere from Manley and Mouldsworth. The " battle and the cannon's smoke were realistic to a degree and quite beyond the power of the rustic mind to grasp, and probably some of them had their moments of doubt as to whether it was not a real sanguinary encounter, " Cease fire sounded in the neighbourhood of Manley. the invaders having at this time taken some 50 or 60 prisoners. The actual issue of the engagement and the fate of the Ship Canal will be announced to-morrow after the conference of umpires.

The Blue, or invading force consisted of the Ist Dragoon Guards, a Equadron of cavalry, the company of mounted infantry, and two guns of the Royal trield Artillery. The Reds comprised all the other regiments. The operations were continued on Tuesday, under the Supervision of Id ajer-General Elal lam Parr, commanding the North-Western Military District. Altogether about 1,100 troops are engaged. The general idea of Tuesday's scheme was similar to that of the previous day the venue of the fighting " being changed to an area between Delamer Frodsham, and Mouldsvrarth. A hostile raiding force (Blue) was supposed to have effected a landing in North Wales and secured the passages of the Dee at Chester, with a view to striking a blow at Manchester and the Ship Canal. A Red force was concentrated about North- wich to check the movement. The Red force, or home defenders, ascertained that the enemy's main columns were moving from Chester to Frodsham, and they advanced from the Yeti, where they commanded I the railway at Mouldsworth Junction, to endeav- our to gain a position where they might threaten or attack the flank of the enemy aril arrest his march. An advance force of the enemy were instructed by the general officer commanding at Chester to make their hold on the high ground about Now Pale, and to protect the advance of the main force and to prevent their march being interfered with. An engagement occurred within the area indicated, and at the conclusion the Reds,or home defendants,had effected their purpose. The Red force consisted of one battalion of Infantry, four guns of the Royal Field Artillery, Yeomanry, and Volunteer details. The Blue force was compcsed of one squadron of cavalry, one company of The eunßtleude liiiofracnetry4hao wondt,we ais ogudnstityliaslhFinieo baldAard w 0 Artillery. commanded by Major Burrard, R.F.A., with Captain Weir, 3rd Dragoon Guards, as chief staff officer. The commander of the Red force was Colonel Ommaney , (commandior 22nd Regimental District), with Captain Thomas, Adjutant 2nd V.B.C.H. The umpires were, Major Oxley, D. A.A.G., and Captain Ward S.C, R.A. ; Lieut.-Colonel Bland, 0.C.,R.A., and Captain Graham, Adjutant, stl v.x, Liverpool Regi- ment (Red). The operations were directed by Major H Crauford, D.A.A.G.

IVARRINGTON:TECHNICAL INSTITUTE. The Syliabus. Mr. Charles Madeley, the secretary oi the Municipal Technical Institute, ties mu issued the syllabus tor 1902-3. It is in pamphlet form and can be obtained at the Museum for one penny. It coctains all information relative to the Continuation School,Commercial Evening School, Technical School, Pupil Teachers' Centre, School of Art and University Extension Lecturer. The new building which is in course of erection in Palmyra-square is nearly finished, and the Science and Technical Glasses will be removed into it early in the Session. Meanwbile, work will be commenced as usual at tee School of Science, Old Barracks, and at the School of Art. Organised courses of instruction have ben arranged in engineering (including building and electricity), chemistry (including manufacture of iron and Eteel),and commercial knowledge, with corresponding preparatory causes in the Continuation School. All students enter- ing will in future be required to pursue the course appropriate`jto their employment, and large reduction of fees will be made in succeeding years to those who by regular attendance and steady work shew their intention to benefit by the instruction provided. In connection with these courses additional subjects have been added to the time table, including practical mechanics, advanced commercial science, and a class in plumbing to replace the one hitherto carried on by the Lancashire County Council. Advanced book- keeping and commercial science classes will be held an Monday evenings, instead of Tuesday as stated in the list of classes. The fees show a considerable reduction on those hither- to charged. The fee tor the continuation school has also been lowered, and a return of one half the amount did will take the place of the attendance prizes hither- to given. ' Attention is called to the Technical scholarships tenable by youths engaged in trades in which artistic skill is required, which are offered for the first time under the Middleton Trust. A course of University Extension Lectures, on " English Prose Writets of the XlXth Century," will be delivered by Mr J C Powys, M.A. THE CONTINUATION SCHOOL. The courses of instruction at this school are three in number, namely : (1) Preparatory science course— arithmetic, mensuration, writing and composition, free- hand and scale drawing, elements of science. ;2) Pre- paratory Commercial Course—writing and composition, shorthand, arithmetic and geography, (3) Preparatory Domestic Course—English composition and writing, arithmetic, needlework, cookery. The fee for each course is 3d a week or 25 a quarter. Half the fees paid will be returned to each student who makes 100 attend- ances. Admission to the commercial and technical schools will be granted at reduced fees to students who have taken the proper preparatory cowrie and made satisfactory attendances. COMMERCIAL EVENING SCHOOL. An organized course of instruction in commercial Ithowleuge has been arranged in connection with this school- All students entering are required to take up the various subjects in the order named unless specially excused by the Superintendent (Mr R J Hall), or fees must be paid as for single classes without reduction. The course of instruction is as follows : Frani. YEAR: Handwriting, Commercial Geography, English, Shorthand, Arithmetic (junior), Book-keeping and Commercial Science (Preliminary). SECOND YEAR : English (Advanced), Arithmetic (Senior), Shorthand, Commercial Science (Elementary), Book-keeping (Elementary), French. THIRD YEAR: Shorthand, Commercial Science (Ad- vanced), Book-keeping (Advanced), French, Spanish or German. Four:era YEAR :—Shorthand, French, Spanish or German. FEE :—First year, 7s 6J ; or for students who have passed the Preparatory Course,2s 6). Second and third year, 7s 6J ; or for the students who have made not less than 20 attendances in each of three subjects in previous Session, 5 Fourth year, 103, or 7s 63 as above. Single subjects 5s each. The course is sufficient to prepare students for tbe Certificates of " Commercial Knowledge " given try the Union of Lancashire and Cheshire Institutes, and the Victoria University. TECHNICAL SCHeOL. The school (now in course of erection and shortly to be opened) has been designed and arranged to provide ample space and modern appliances for scientific in- struction. It includes accommodation for the following departments:—Chemical laboratory,phyeical laboratory, mechanics laboratory, biological laboratory, drawing office, woodworking shop, metal-working shop, cookery kitchen, dressing-room laundry,with the lecture-rooms and accessories required. A students' reading-room is also provided. Until transferred to the new building the classes in mechanical drawing meet at the Scheel of Art, and the Science classes at the School of Scier ce, Museum-street. The following organized courses of instruction have been arranged. All students entering are required to take up the various subjects in the order specified, or fees must be paid as for single classes,without reduction. Former students will receive due consideration for work already done. MECHANICAL ENGINEERING.—First Year: Practical Geometry, Practical Mathematics, 1 hour, Machine Drawing. Second year : Practc d Mathematics, 2 hours, Machine Drawing, Applied Mechanics, Practical Mechanics. Third year : Applied Mechanics, Practical Mechanics, Steam, or Electricity, Eltctricity Practical, Inorganic Chemistry. Fourth year : Steam, Electricity, Practical Electricity. BUILDING.—First Year : Practical Geometry,Practi- cal Mathematics, Building Construction. Second year : Practical Mathematics, Building Construction, Applied Mechanics. PLummxo.--First Year r Practical Geometry, Practi- cal Mathematics, 1 hour, Plumbers' Work. Second year: Practical Mathematics, Applied Mechanics, Plumbers' Work. Third year : Applied Mechanics, Inorganic Chemistry, Plumbers' Work. CHESIISTRY.—First Year : Mathematic; I, Inorganic Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry (Practical). &Gond year: Inorganic Chemistry, Advanced, Inorganic Chemistry (Practical), Iron and Steel (Optional), Elec- tricity, Theor (Optional). Third year : Inorganic Chemistry, Advanced, Inorganic Chemistry (Practical), or Electricity, Theor* and Practical, Organic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry (Practical). PUPIL TEACHERS' CENTRE. This centre will be conducted at the Technical School as soon as the building is completed. It is a day sehoo designed to give a sound general education to young teachers. Tee pupils are carefully prepared for the King's Scholarship Examination, but the curriculum is so arranged that studetts can also, if desired, take the London University and Cambridge Local exams. Students are required to attend four half-days weekly SCHOOL OF ART. The objects of this school, of which Mr C B Aylward is the headmaster, are to promote the growth of indus- trial art, to make drawing a part of general education, and to train those who desire to follow art as a profes- sion. Subjects of Instruction Elementary.—Geometrical drawing, perspective, freehand drawing of ornament, drawing from models and objects, drawing in lighb and shade from the cast, modelling in clay from casts and natural objects. drawing with chalk on the blackboard. edvanced : Drawing—Advanced Stages of Freehand, Model drawing, and drawing in light and shade. Archi- tecture—Drawing of architectural details. Architectural desien. Linear perspective and eciography. Theory and Designing—Principles and history of ornament. Design, applied to Decorative and Industrial Art, with Special reference to local industries; Painting—Painting in monochreme and colours, in water-colour. tempera, and oil. Painting from nature compositions o Study of the Figure—Drawing and pilal life, flowers, 4e gfiforwomthe4;ntique and from the lire. Artistic anatomy. Life-classes for study from draped models and the nude. Modelling in clay from examples of ornament and from nature modelling design. APPLIED ART.—Work carried out in various materials (such as earthenware, porcelain, glass, metal, wood, textiles) may now be sent up to South Kensington Biotin with the d,tsigns for the same. Special classes are held in wood•carving and Embroidery. TEE OPENING OF THE INSTITUTE. We understand that Lord Derbnhas consentee to open theinew technical institute huildirgs in October. The date has not yet been fixed.
